preamble: The back-gliding diphthong /au/ became the front diphthong /ɛi/ in Faroese. Old Norse au was already rounded and fronted (roughly /ɶu/) in Old West Norse, merged with the i-umlauted diphthong øy, and at the beginning of the 14th century the whole series was delabialized (y, øy, au > /i, ɔi, ɛi/). Modern Faroese spells the result ey. No comparable direct au > ei change is well documented outside this branch, so the shift is rare.

examples.note: Old Norse au corresponds regularly to Faroese ey, pronounced [ɛi].
